timestep_s.why: MuJoCo step; the headline runs are repeated at 0.001 s as a numerical check

floor_friction.why: assumed: printed PLA sole on a table top, as in the first model; sensitivity is reported from 0.3 to 1.0

contact_timeconst_s.why: assumed: stiff floor contact (MuJoCo solref); the default 0.02 lets a sole sink about 0.3 mm, which is the size of the clearances measured here

transport_delay_ms.why: assumed: one controller tick for a command line to cross the USB or bridge link and be parsed

controller_tick_ms.why: the firmware loop (microduck/protocol.py); commands are also rate limited there

pwm_latency_ms.why: the servo reads one pulse per 50 Hz frame, so a new target is acted on one frame after the controller sets it

pulse_resolution_us.why: the firmware rounds the pulse width to a whole microsecond, 0.09 degrees

deadband_deg.why: assumed: an 8 microsecond dead band, typical for an analog servo; the maker publishes none

backlash_deg.why: assumed: total gear play at the horn, typical for a plastic or mixed gear train. The feedback potentiometer is on the output shaft, so play adds to the zone in which the servo does not push back: half of it each side

full_torque_error_deg.why: assumed in the first model: the servo reaches stall torque this far outside the dead zone

flex_nm_per_rad.why: assumed: series spring between horn and link for the cable-tied case, the plastic horn and the 4 mm plate; about 1.5 degrees at stall torque. Not sensed by the servo

flex_damping_nms_per_rad.why: assumed: light damping of that spring

supply_current_a.why: published: the Braccio supply is 5 V 4 A. When the estimated current of the six servos exceeds it all torques are scaled down together. Stall currents are assumed (config/hardware.json)

relaxed_friction_nm.why: assumed in the first model: friction of an unpowered gear train. Rest poses are also checked with zero friction

sole_sag_mm.why: the soles are rigid in the model. The part generator computes 0.5 mm (PLA) to 0.9 mm (PETG) of sag at the centre line with the whole weight on one foot; the series spring per joint is the only compliance here

head._comment: A point mass added to the torso so results can be rerun for a heavier or different head. Zero means the torso as generated in robot/microduck.xml, which already carries the default head (display 15 g, camera 10 g).

max_speed_deg_s.why: the default in config/calibration.json; walk, turn, sit and stand stay inside it

jump_max_speed_deg_s.why: the jump needs the firmware rate limit raised to the no-load speed of the faster servo; the servo model still limits each joint to its published speed

robot_presets.comb: The robot as generated: comb soles whose fingers cross the centre line.
robot_presets.flat_feet: Comparison: the same robot with the flat sole plates as first drawn (75 by 48 by 5 mm) in place of the comb soles, the hip roll limits those soles had, and no leg clearance rule.
